## Summary

The spec required emitting an `AUDIT` log line on successful owner creation containing the owner id, `customerCode`, and `registrationDate`. The `Owner` model already carried and exposed both fields, so only the audit side-effect was missing.

To keep structural impact low, I avoided growing the large `addOwner` controller method (whose class carries high surrounding complexity). Instead I added the behaviour as a small, self-contained unit:

- **New file** `model/OwnerAuditListener.java` — a JPA `@PostPersist` entity listener with a single trivial method (no surrounding methods, so zero contextual complexity) that logs to the `AUDIT` logger.
- **One-line change** to `Owner.java` — a class-level `@EntityListeners(OwnerAuditListener.class)` annotation (no existing function modified; `@EntityListeners` was already covered by the wildcard `jakarta.persistence.*` import).

The listener fires only on genuine inserts of a new owner (household re-saves of existing owners are merges and don't trigger `@PostPersist`), by which point the id, `customerCode`, and `registrationDate` are all set — matching the "on successful create" requirement.
